title: Discussion 5: Trees & Mutual Recursion
description: A discussion worksheet on the Tree ADT: tracing recursive functions over trees before verifying your prediction.

questions.title: tree_sum
questions.prompt:
Trace tree_sum(t), which returns the sum of all labels in t.

>>> t = Tree(1, [Tree(2), Tree(3)])
>>> tree_sum(t)
questions.starter_code:
def tree_sum(t):
    return t.label + sum([tree_sum(b) for b in t.branches])

questions.title: tree_map
questions.prompt:
Implement tree_map(fn, t), which returns a new tree where fn has been applied to every entry in t, preserving structure.

>>> t = Tree(1, [Tree(2), Tree(3)])
>>> tree_map(lambda x: x * 2, t)
questions.starter_code:
def tree_map(fn, t):
    return Tree(fn(t.label), [tree_map(fn, c) for c in t.branches])

questions.title: tree_contains
questions.prompt:
Trace tree_contains(t, value), which returns whether value appears anywhere in t.

>>> t = Tree(1, [Tree(2), Tree(3, [Tree(4)])])
>>> tree_contains(t, 4)

questions.title: height
questions.prompt:
Trace height(t), which returns the height of tree t (a leaf has height 0).

>>> t = Tree(1, [Tree(2, [Tree(3)]), Tree(4)])
>>> height(t)

questions.title: leaves
questions.prompt:
Trace leaves(t), which returns a list of the labels of all leaf nodes (nodes with no branches) in t, left to right.

>>> t = Tree(1, [Tree(2, [Tree(3), Tree(4)]), Tree(5)])
>>> leaves(t)
